title: Аврал в зале и приход режиссёра  (Dining Room Crisis and the Director's Arrival)

segments.t: With Nastya overwhelmed in the dining room, impatient customers begin demanding to speak to the manager about their delayed orders. At that exact moment, the celebrated arthouse film director walks through the entrance—turning out to be the very same older woman Max had been cooking for.
Девушка, когда вы уже принесете мой заказ?
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Hello, Kostyan.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'hello' before landing on 'Kostyan'.
'In five minutes?' Chef Viktor raises the pitch on 'minutes' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Vika answers right away.
'Right this way, please.' The grammar packs 'beg' and 'you' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Девушка, когда вы уже принесете мой заказ?
'Miss, when are you finally going to bring my order?' In Russian, the idea of 'girl' flows naturally into 'order' without extra filler words.
'Right away, just one moment.' The meaning hinges on 'any minute' working together with 'a minute' in spoken Russian. Vika answers right away.
'I am working on your salad right now.' In Russian, the idea of 'work' flows naturally into 'salad' without extra filler words.
'Enjoy your meal.' Max anchors the line on 'pleasant', while 'appetite' completes the thought.
'Go ahead and call the manager then.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'and' and finishing on 'call'. Vika answers right away.
'Everything is in order, everything is great.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'all' before landing on 'great!'.
'Is the table ready for me?' The grammar packs 'table' and 'ready' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'We will prepare everything this very second.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'we' and finishing on 'to prepare'. Vika answers right away.
'What did you want, an autograph?' The grammar packs 'what' and 'autograph' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Very good indeed.' The meaning hinges on 'very' working together with 'fine' in spoken Russian. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
